title: 1975 AHSME Problem 28
statement: In triangle \(ABC\) shown in the adjoining figure, \(M\) is the midpoint of side \(BC,\) \(AB=12,\) and \(AC=16.\) Points \(E\) and \(F\) are taken on \(AC\) and \(AB,\) respectively, and lines \(EF\) and \(AM\) intersect at \(G.\) If \(AE=2AF,\) then \(\frac{EG}{GF}\) equals

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: not enough information given to solve the problem

solutions.text:
Put \(A\) at the origin and write the position vectors of \(B,C\) as \(\mathbf b,\mathbf c.\) If \(F=t\mathbf b,\) then \(AF=12t\) and \(AE=24t,\) so \(E=(\frac{3t}{2})\mathbf c.\) Write \(G=(1-u)F+uE.\) Because \(G\) also lies on the median \(AM,\) its \(\mathbf b\) and \(\mathbf c\) coefficients are equal: \[ (1-u)t=\frac32ut. \] Hence \(u=\frac{2}{5}.\) Along \(FE,\frac{FG}{FE}=\frac{2}{5}\) and \(\frac{EG}{FE}=\frac{3}{5},\) so \(\frac{EG}{GF}=\frac{3}{2}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Represent \(B,C\) by vectors \(\mathbf b,\mathbf c\) from \(A\)
If \(F=t\mathbf b,\) then \(E=\frac32t\mathbf c;\) equate the \(\mathbf b,\mathbf c\) coefficients of a point on \(EF\) and on \(AM\)
